Integrity

/in-TEG-ri-tee/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Integrity is quality of being moral or whole.

She earned everyone's trust because of her honesty and integrity.

Worked Example

An accountant discovers that a small error of her own accidentally awarded her a larger bonus. No audit would ever catch it, yet she reports the mistake the next morning and returns the money.

She does the right thing even when no one is watching and even at a cost to herself — that moral wholeness is integrity. Integrity is more precise than 'honesty' because it names a complete, consistent character, not just a single truthful act.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

honesty: Honesty is telling the truth and avoiding lies. Integrity is a broader character trait. It means your actions match your moral values, even when no one is watching. Honesty is about your words, while integrity is about your whole character and consistency.

uprightness: Uprightness is consistently moral, principled behavior — an upright person visibly follows the rules of right conduct. Integrity goes a layer deeper: it is the inner wholeness that keeps you the same person in private as in public, even when no rule or witness demands it.

probity: Probity is honesty that has been tested and proven — the formal word for a spotless record, especially with money or public office. Integrity is the broader everyday character trait behind such a record: whole, consistent moral conduct in everything, not only in matters that get audited.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

dishonesty: the practice of lying or deceiving

corruption: dishonest abuse of power for gain

Where it sits · how fully your principles hold up — decency → sincerity → integrity → incorruptibility

decency vs. integrity: Decency is weaker than integrity — decency means meeting basic standards of good behavior, while integrity means being morally whole in everything you do.

sincerity vs. integrity: Sincerity is weaker than integrity — a sincere person genuinely means what they say in the moment, while a person of integrity backs those words with consistently moral action in everything they do.

incorruptibility vs. integrity: Incorruptibility is stronger than integrity — a person of integrity does the right thing, while an incorruptible person cannot be tempted to do otherwise, no matter the pressure.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — integr

root — integr: whole, untouched (Latin (integer))

suffix — -ity

suffix — -ity: state or quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Integr (whole — from Latin integer, 'untouched,' built from in- 'not' + tangere 'to touch') + -ity (quality of): integrity is the quality of being morally whole — unbroken and undivided, like an untouched whole.

Use the root in a new word: integrate

Use the root in a new word: integrate: The new student integrated quickly into the class.

Root Check

Word Choice

Integrity most often describes a person's steady honesty and strong moral principles (a leader of great integrity), but can also describe something's structural soundness (the integrity of a bridge) — both senses share the idea of being whole and unbroken.
